messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
मैं इसे कैसे प्रवेश किया यह मैं ठीक से नहीं बता सकता, उस बिंदु पर मैं अत्यधिक नींद से भर गया था जहाँ मैंने सच्चा मार्ग छोड़ दिया।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (all three lines combined)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Io | 1st‑person singular pronoun (subject) | मैं | I | OK | | non | Negation particle | नहीं | not | OK | | so | Verb *sapere* “to know” (present 1sg) | बता | tell / know (as in “cannot tell”) | OK | | ben | Adverb of manner “well” | ठीक से | properly, well | OK | | ridir | Infinitive “to recount, tell again” | बता | tell, recount | OK | | com' | Interrogative adverb “how” | कैसे | how | OK | | i' | Clitic pronoun “I” (re‑iteration inside clause) | — (subject already expressed by मैं) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | v'intrai | Past historic “entered it” | इसे प्रवेश किया | entered it | OK | | tant' | Degree adverb “so, such” | अत्यधिक | extremely, so | OK | | era | Imperfect “was” (3sg) | था | was | OK | | pien | Predicative adjective “full” | भर गया | became full / was full | OK | | di | Preposition “of” linking adjective to noun | से | of / from | OK | | sonno | Noun “slumber, sleepiness” | नींद | sleep, slumber | OK | | a | Preposition “at” (temporal) | पर | at, on | OK | | quel | Demonstrative adjective “that” | उस | that | OK | | punto | Noun “point, moment” | बिंदु | point, moment | OK | | che | Relative conjunction “where” | जहाँ | where | OK | | la | Definite article (feminine singular) | — (articles omitted in Hindi) | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | verace | Adjective “true, genuine” | सच्चा | true, genuine | OK | | via | Noun “way, path” | मार्ग | way, path | OK | | abbandonai | Past historic “abandoned” | छोड़ दिया | abandoned, left | OK |
### Summary of Issues - **UNNECESSARY**: `i'` (clitic pronoun) – Hindi already marks the subject with *मैं*; `la` (definite article) – Hindi does not use articles. - **MISSING**: none. - **WRONG**: none. - **GRAMMAR**: none detected; the Hindi rendering respects gender, number, and tense.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 10** - Original: मैं इसे कैसे प्रवेश किया यह मैं ठीक से नहीं बता सकता, - Issue: none - Corrected: मैं इसे कैसे प्रवेश किया, ठीक से नहीं बता सकता,
- **Line 11** - Original: उस बिंदु पर मैं अत्यधिक नींद से भर गया था - Issue: none - Corrected: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं
- **Line 12** - Original: जहाँ मैंने सच्चा मार्ग छोड़ दिया। - Issue: none - Corrected: कोई परिवर्तन नहीं
